summary: Runs 1 and 2 (BrickWork Pro, non-VAT and VAT) read as credible construction sole-trader accounts. Run 3 (Precision Code advanced) does not: the fixed asset additions and capital allowances of £32,500 do not match the £39,000 fa-coded capital spending in the journal (and the VAT-net equivalent of £32,500 is what the checks assume), the P&L cost-of-sales carries only £16,137 against sales of £339,200 with no stock movement reflected despite opening stock £10,000 / closing £6,000, and the SA103S taxable profit (£146,632) disagrees with the profit actually taxed (£148,715).

concerns.figure: Capital allowances / fixed asset additions 32,500 vs scenario fa-coded capital spending 39,000
concerns.where: Run 3 (se-scenario-advanced): SE Short D80, Fixedassets.xlsx!FAreconciliation E11/E13, Schedule Q1
concerns.why: The purchase journal states 39,000.00 coded fa. Journal amounts are VAT-inclusive, so the net capitalised figure should be 32,500 only if the whole 39,000 is standard-rated — which is consistent — but the report's own compliance line labels 32,500 as 'scenario fa-coded net total'. The reader should confirm the fa treatment, because the two other runs in this batch capitalise 12,000 net against 12,000 gross (non-VAT) and 12,000 net against 14,400 gross (VAT), so the VAT treatment of fa purchases is applied inconsistently across the shipped scenarios.

concerns.figure: SA103S Taxable profit 146,632.06 vs Net profit for tax calc 148,715.39 and Income Tax E5 148,715.39
concerns.where: Run 3: SE Short D99 vs D106, and Income Tax E5
concerns.why: The SA103S taxable profit line and the profit actually carried into the income tax computation differ by 2,083.33 — exactly the Grants Received figure. One of the two is wrong; a reader of the tax return cannot tell which profit is being declared, and tax of £51,148.86 is charged on the higher of the two.

concerns.figure: Cost of Sales 16,136.67 against Sales Turnover 339,200 (gross profit 95.9%), with no stock movement
concerns.why: The scenario states opening stock 10,000 and closing stock 6,000, so a 4,000 stock decrease should increase cost of sales, yet Materials/Stock is 5,450 (the s-coded net figure alone) and no stock adjustment appears anywhere. For a consultancy a thin cost of sales is plausible, but the declared stock movement has gone missing from the accounts entirely.

concerns.figure: Purchases net of VAT 92,493.54 in the VAT Returns section vs 71,992.25 revenue spending + 39,000 capital stated in the scenario
concerns.where: Run 3: VAT Returns block (Purchases invoiced including VAT 110,992.25, net 92,493.54)
concerns.why: 110,992.25 divided by 1.2 is 92,493.54, which treats every purchase including the fa items as standard-rated, while the P&L and fixed asset schedule net down only part of it. Worth checking that input VAT of 18,498.71 is genuinely all recoverable on the mix described.

concerns.where: Run 3: P&L B29 (and N29 monthly column)
concerns.why: A negative bad debt charge in the admin expenses block reduces expenses. It is small, but the sign should be confirmed as a genuine bad-debt recovery rather than a coding error on the o-coded sales entry.

concerns.figure: Total Tax + NI 0 on Profit Before Tax 14,830
concerns.why: Nil tax follows correctly from taxable profit of 4,030 after the 12,000 capital allowance claim and the 12,570 personal allowance, so this is not an error — but a reader should note the whole 12,000 of fixed assets was relieved in year one, leaving accounting depreciation of 1,200 and no tax charge at all.
